item.title: Team returns with pride | A gold medal, a bronze and a historic first in swimming
item.description: TEAM Fiji returned from the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games with a gold medal, a bronze medal and a historic first in swimming after a memorable campaign highlighted by weightlifter Taniela Tuisuva Rainibogi, swimmer David Young and boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama. item.content:encoded:
TEAM Fiji returned from the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games with a gold medal, a bronze medal and a historic first in swimming after a memorable campaign highlighted by weightlifter Taniela Tuisuva Rainibogi, swimmer David Young and boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama.

Rainibogi produced Fiji’s greatest moment of the Games when he claimed gold in the men’s 110kg weightlifting competition on Thursday, July 30.

The Fijian powerhouse delivered a record-breaking performance, lifting 170kg in the snatch, 208kg in the clean and jerk and finishing with a total of 378kg.

All three lifts were Commonwealth Games records, making Rainibogi the first Fijian athlete to win gold at Glasgow 2026 and adding another chapter to Fiji’s weightlifting success on the international stage.

By the closing of the Games on Sunday, August 2, Daunakamakama had secured Fiji’s second medal after winning bronze in the women’s 57kg boxing division.

Daunakamakama defeated Ghana’s Adelaide Dede Djabatey 5-0 in the quarter-final and Sri Lanka’s Keshani Hansika 4-1 in the last eight before her semi-final loss to Northern Ireland’s Michaela Walsh.

Her bronze medal performance capped a strong tournament for Fiji’s boxing team.

Meanwhile, David Young created history in the swimming pool by becoming the first Fijian swimmer to reach a Commonwealth Games final.

Young progressed through the men’s 50m freestyle after recording 22.16 seconds in the heats and improving to 22.09 seconds in the semi-final.

In the final, he clocked 22.18 seconds to finish sixth against some of the best swimmers in the Commonwealth.

He also competed in the 100m freestyle, finishing 26th in 50.84 seconds, and the 50m butterfly where he recorded 24.28 seconds.

Fiji’s swimmers continued to make history with several national records broken throughout the competition.

Anahira McCutcheon set a new Fiji record in the women’s 100m freestyle with a time of 55.80 seconds in the semi-final, while also reaching the semi-final of the 50m freestyle and finishing 12th in the 50m butterfly.

Samuel Yalimaiwai also broke the national record in the men’s 50m breaststroke with a time of 28.23 seconds in the semi-final.

The men’s 4x100m medley relay team of Reuben Taylor, Yalimaiwai, Hansel McCaig and Young finished 13th with a time of 4:02.77, while the mixed 4x100m medley relay team placed 16th.

In athletics, Rusiate Matai produced a season’s best performance of 2.05m in the men’s high jump final to finish ninth.

Heleina Young recorded season’s best times in the women’s 200m heats, clocking 24.45 seconds after competing in the 100m heats, while Errol Qaqa ran 14.66 seconds in the men’s 110m hurdles.

Yeshnil Karan also achieved a season’s best in the men’s one mile with a time of 4:12.28.

Sitiveni Konataci finished ninth in the men’s discus F42-44/F61-64 final with a season’s best throw of 27.54m.

In bowls, Rajnesh Prasad impressed in the men’s singles, recording three wins from five matches and finishing fourth in Section C. He defeated England’s Sam Tolchard and overcame Scotland’s Jason Banks in a tie-break.

Litia Tikoisuva and Losalini Tukai recorded victories over Botswana and Kenya in the women’s pairs, while Lal Chand Prasad and Surendra Prasad also competed strongly in the men’s pairs.

Judoka Gerard Takayawa finished seventh in the men’s over 100kg category after defeating Northern Ireland’s Adam Hall by ippon before bowing out in the quarter-final and repechage stages.

Fiji’s 3×3 basketball teams also gained valuable experience, with the men recording a win against Jamaica while competing in Pool B, and the women facing Uganda and Jamaica in Pool A.

Apakuki Wakanibua finished ninth in the men’s 65kg weightlifting category with a total lift of 215kg.

Team Fiji’s Glasgow 2026 journey will be remembered for Rainibogi’s record-breaking gold medal, Daunakamakama’s boxing bronze and Young’s historic swimming achievement.

The team also acknowledged the contribution of coaches, team managers, medical staff, national sporting federations, families and volunteers who supported the athletes throughout the Games.

With a gold medal, a bronze medal, national swimming records and a historic Commonwealth Games swimming final appearance, Team Fiji returns home with pride and renewed confidence for the future.

item.title: FRU backs match officials | On-field decision final
item.description: THE Fiji Rugby Union (FRU) has defended the match officials involved in the controversial Vodafone Deans Under-18 elimination clash between Queen Victoria School (QVS) and Ba Provincial Freebird Institute at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka last Saturday. The match between the two rugby powerhouses sparked widespread debate after video footage circulated on social media appeared to show a successful QVS co
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Rugby Union (FRU) has defended the match officials involved in the controversial Vodafone Deans Under-18 elimination clash between Queen Victoria School (QVS) and Ba Provincial Freebird Institute at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka last Saturday.

The match between the two rugby powerhouses sparked widespread debate after video footage circulated on social media appeared to show a successful QVS conversion that was not awarded by the assistant referee, a decision many believe had a significant impact on the result of the game.

Speaking to Times Sport, FRU acting chief operating officer Talemo Waqa said the union’s position is guided by World Rugby laws.

FRU insisted that under World Rugby regulations, on-field decisions cannot be overturned.

“The official opinion is similar to World Rugby. All field decisions of the referee, the TMO and the assistant referees always stand. We cannot overrule them from an administration side or from outside of that,” Waqa said.

He explained that the FRU cannot rely on videos recorded by spectators or parents when reviewing matches.

“These are viral videos taken by parents or spectators, so we really cannot use those kinds of videos whenever we are reviewing. Even if we review television footage afterwards, we still cannot change the on-field decision.”

2026 Vodafone Super Deans Trophy Under-18 fixtures:

Ra High School v Ratu Kadavulevu School at 1.40pm; and

Cuvu College v Nasinu Secondary School at 3.05pm.

Lelean Memorial School v Ratu Navula College at 4.30pm; and

Suva Grammar School v Ba Provincial Freebird Institute at 5.55pm.

item.description: THE Springboks and Fiji Airways Fijiana XV clash marks the first-time the South African women’s side has played a Test on Fijian soil. South Africa vice-captain Libbie Janse van Rensburg said the opportunity to travel to Fiji and face the Fijiana XV was something that would have seemed unlikely just a few years ago, highlighting how far the women’s game had progressed internationally.
item.content:encoded:
THE Springboks and Fiji Airways Fijiana XV clash marks the first-time the South African women’s side has played a Test on Fijian soil.

South Africa vice-captain Libbie Janse van Rensburg said the opportunity to travel to Fiji and face the Fijiana XV was something that would have seemed unlikely just a few years ago, highlighting how far the women’s game had progressed internationally.

“I think it’s absolutely amazing just to see the growth of women’s rugby, where we’ve come to know,” she said.

She hopes the historic fixture will pave the way for more international Tests between the two nations and further strengthen the women’s game around the world.

item.title: Walker ready to unlock Fijiana’s potential
item.description: NEWLY appointed Vodafone Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker is looking forward to the challenge of guiding Fiji’s women’s national 15s team, believing the side has the talent and potential to compete at the highest level of world rugby. Walker, who has enjoyed success coaching championship-winning teams and developing players, who have gone on to represent the Black Ferns and sevens rugby at the
item.content:encoded:
NEWLY appointed Vodafone Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker is looking forward to the challenge of guiding Fiji’s women’s national 15s team, believing the side has the talent and potential to compete at the highest level of world rugby.

Walker, who has enjoyed success coaching championship-winning teams and developing players, who have gone on to represent the Black Ferns and sevens rugby at the international stage, says his coaching philosophy has always centred around serving his players and creating an environment where they can succeed.

“For me as a coach, it’s about service and making sure that I do everything I can to make sure that the players get what they need to be successful,” Walker said.

“At the end of the day, that’s where I get my pleasure from, seeing my players succeed.”

Walker brings years of experience working with talented athletes and hopes to share his knowledge to help the Fijiana players continue their growth and make their mark in world rugby.

“I’ve been lucky, I’ve had a really good group of players over the years that have developed into World Cup winners, Black Ferns, multiple Black Ferns and sevens players that have stamped their mark on world rugby,” he said.

“I’m hoping to be able to share some of my knowledge so that our Fijiana girls are in that same step and we just continue to grow and push.”

The new head coach said one of his key priorities would be combining the natural ability of Fijian players with the standards and expectations required at the professional level.

Walker believes Fiji’s rugby talent provides an exciting opportunity, but improving the basics and fundamentals will be crucial to achieving success.

“The potential that this country has in terms of rugby is exciting,” he said.

“I think it’s an exciting thing to have that natural ability to play rugby, play an expansive game, be powerful and strong.”

“If we can fine tune some of that and get some of the fundamentals and basics sorted out, then there’s a really good opportunity to see some pretty quick growth in this game.”

Walker said the challenge of developing the Fijiana XV was one of the biggest attractions of taking up the role, as he looked to build on the team’s progress and help establish Fiji as a stronger force in international women’s rugby.

The Vodafone Fijiana XV will face the Springboks Women this Saturday at 2pm at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

item.title: Springboks eager to make history
item.description: THE Springboks Women have quickly overcome the fatigue of a long journey to Fiji and are eager to make history in their first Test match on Fijian soil against the Vodafone Fijiana XV at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva this Saturday. Vice-captain Libbie Janse van Rensburg said the squad had recovered well and was now fully focused on the challenge ahead.
item.content:encoded:
THE Springboks Women have quickly overcome the fatigue of a long journey to Fiji and are eager to make history in their first Test match on Fijian soil against the Vodafone Fijiana XV at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva this Saturday.

Vice-captain Libbie Janse van Rensburg said the squad had recovered well and was now fully focused on the challenge ahead.

“We’ve had quite a long journey to get here, but the team has settled in well,” she said.

“We’ve had a couple of days to recuperate, get our energy back up and hit the ground running with our first training session. The morale is really good, the energy is looking good, and we’re really excited for the game on Saturday.”

While South Africa suffered a defeat to Fiji at the 2002 Women’s Rugby World Cup, Janse van Rensburg said that result no longer played a part in the team’s mindset.

“So many years have passed and women’s rugby has grown tremendously since then.

“Some players were part of that era, but many of our squad are new.

“We’ve also gone through another World Cup cycle since then, so we’re not dwelling on the past.

“We’re focused on building on the success we’ve had in recent years.”

She expects Fiji to provide a stern test.

“We know Fiji always brings physicality. They like to play fast and with a lot of freedom.

“It will be interesting to see how our physicality matches up against theirs.

“We’re also known for being a dominant team, so I think it’s going to be a fantastic game and a great showcase for everyone coming to watch.”

She also acknowledged the influence of the world champion Springbok men’s team, saying their achievements have inspired the women’s program.

“A lot of our ladies look up to what the men’s team has achieved over the past few years.

“They’ve had their challenges as well, but the success they’ve enjoyed has been incredibly inspirational for us.”

Janse van Rensburg said the support from senior Springboks, including captain Siya Kolisi, had given the women’s team extra motivation.

“To know the men are backing us and to have people like Siya Kolisi come to our training and support the women’s game is incredible”, she said.

The first Test match between the Springbok Women and the Vodafone Fijiana XV will kick off at 2.05pm this Saturday at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

item.title: ‘Collision wins Tests’
item.description: THE Fijiana XVs are sharpening their physical game ahead of this weekend’s Test match against the Springbok Women, with interim head coach Mike Legge identifying the collision area as the team’s top priority. The national side resumed training this week as players continued assembling in camp, giving the coaching staff time to fine-tune combinations before Saturday’s clash. Legge noted that lesson
item.content:encoded:
THE Fijiana XVs are sharpening their physical game ahead of this weekend’s Test match against the Springbok Women, with interim head coach Mike Legge identifying the collision area as the team’s top priority.

The national side resumed training this week as players continued assembling in camp, giving the coaching staff time to fine-tune combinations before Saturday’s clash. Legge noted that lessons learned from their Super Rugby Women’s final defeat to the NSW Waratahs have directly shaped their preparations.

“Our big focus this week is the collision,” Legge said. “What we learnt from losing the final against the Waratahs was making sure we win the collision. South Africa is a big team. I don’t think the girls would have come up against a team the size of South Africa before.”

He acknowledged the stern test awaiting them on the pitch. “It’s going to be a massive, massive challenge for us,” he said.

While a few players are still expected to arrive in camp, the interim head coach expressed confidence that the squad will be fully prepared. He added that South Africa will provide a rigorous test after building momentum in recent international fixtures.

“They’ve had a good test series against the US, which was recent. They’re a team that’s slowly building in.

“These girls wouldn’t have come up against a size like that. Probably the physicality, but it’s going to be a good challenge for us.”

Despite the emphasis on matching South Africa’s size and power, Legge insisted Fiji will not stray from its signature flair.

“We want to continue our style of game,” Legge said.

“So, we’ll work hard on the collision, work hard on what we do on the edges as well. It’s going to be pretty much similar to how we played the last couple of months.”

Although a few squad members are currently on modified training programs following the Super Rugby Women’s final, they are expected to return to full training shortly.

“Some of our girls are still carrying some injuries from the Super final. So, they’re only doing some modified stuff today, but they’ll be back for training.”

With the Test taking place at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, Legge is calling on local fans to turn out in full force.

“We have our core group of supporters that continue to follow us where we go. I know they’ll show up in numbers on Saturday, but also, we’re hoping that the Dean’s parents remain and support our girls as well. I think it’s going to be a really good game. Two very different styles of rugby.”

item.content:encoded:
THE race for the Vodafone Super Deans Trophy has reached the knockout stage, with secondary schools across Fiji confirming their places in the national quarter-finals after another thrilling weekend of rugby action.

In the premier Under-18 grade, southern giants Suva Grammar School once again stamped their authority with a commanding playoff performance to secure a quarter-final berth. They will be joined by Nasinu Secondary School, who edged out their opponents in a hard-fought encounter to keep their title hopes alive.

• Under-14: Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School (MGM), Suva Grammar School (SGS), Nasinu Secondary School (NSS):

• Under-15: SGS, Marist Brothers High School (MBHS), NSS:

• Under-17: SGS, Gospel High School, MBHS:

• Under-19: SGS, NSS, Ratu Simione Matanitobua College

In the Eastern Division, unbeaten Lelean Memorial School continued its impressive campaign and will be joined by Ratu Kadavulevu School in the Under-18 national quarter-finals.

Queen Victoria School, Ratu Kadavulevu School and Lelean Memorial School also secured qualification in the Under-14, Under-15, Under-16 and Under-17 grades. In the Under-19 division, RKS and Lelean will be joined by Navatu Secondary School.

The Western Division celebrated a significant achievement, with four schools advancing to the Under-18 quarter-finals.

Ra High School, Ba Provincial Freebird Institute, Cuvu College and Ratu Navula College all booked their places after strong performances in the elimination round.

• Under-14: Ratu Navula College, Nadi Muslim College:

• Under-15: Natabua High: School, Ba Methodist High School

• Under-16: Cuvu College, Ratu Navula College:

• Under-17: Ba Methodist High School, Sigatoka Methodist College: and

• Under-19: Ratu Navula College, Xavier College.

Meanwhile, the Weet-Bix Raluve Championship Under-16 quarter-finals will feature Adi Cakobau School, St Vincent College, Bucalevu Secondary School, Nabala Secondary School, Nasinu Secondary School, Suva Grammar School, Sigatoka Methodist College and St Theresa’s High School.

The Weet-Bix Raluve Under-18 competition will include Sila Central High School, Adi Cakobau School, St Bedes College, Bucalevu Secondary School, Lomary Secondary School, Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School, defending champions Jasper Williams High School and last year’s runners-up Natabua High School.

With traditional powerhouses and emerging challengers still in contention, the stage is set for another electrifying weekend of schools rugby.

Every match now carries added significance as teams battle for a coveted place in the national semi-finals, with months of preparation and sacrifice on the line.

item.title: Wairabetia school claims back-to-back U14 soccer title
item.description: WAIRABETIA Muslim Primary School successfully defended its under-14 soccer title after producing an unbeaten campaign in the Tabua Grade at the Lautoka Inter-primary schools Soccer competition held at Central Primary Ground last weekend. Led by head boy and captain Napolioni Waqatabu, the young side showed determination and discipline to secure back-to-back championship honours.
item.content:encoded:
WAIRABETIA Muslim Primary School successfully defended its under-14 soccer title after producing an unbeaten campaign in the Tabua Grade at the Lautoka Inter-primary schools Soccer competition held at Central Primary Ground last weekend.

Led by head boy and captain Napolioni Waqatabu, the young side showed determination and discipline to secure back-to-back championship honours.

Wairabetia opened its campaign with two scoreless draws against Dreketi Sangam Primary and Tuvu Primary before finding its rhythm in the third match with a convincing 2-0 victory over Qalitu Primary. The goals came from Mateo Draunimasi of Year 8 and captain Waqatabu.

The semi-final proved to be another hard-fought contest as Wairabetia edged Satya Sai Primary 1-0. Goalkeeper Cama Veiqaravi emerged as the hero after producing a crucial penalty save, while Waqatabu scored the decisive goal to send his side into the final.

In the championship match, Wairabetia once again defeated Tuvu Primary 2-0 to lift the title. Waqatabu continued his outstanding form by finding the back of the net, while Year 6 student Isoa Musuqio added the second goal to seal the victory.

The team was guided by coach Imraan Iqbal, a former Fiji Football Association referee, whose experience played a key role in the school’s successful title defence.

Meanwhile, Wairabetia Muslim Primary’s under-14 girls also made an encouraging debut in the tournament, impressing against more experienced opponents. Goalkeeper Banikarawa Mita, who hails from Rabi, highlighted the team’s performance with a brilliant penalty save.

The girls were coached by Aachal Narayan, who praised the team’s effort and commitment throughout the competition.

Following their successful outing, Wairabetia Muslim Primary will now shift their focus to the Northwest Primary Schools Soccer Competition in Term Three, which will be held in Ba after the Fiji Year Eight Examination, where both teams will be eager to continue building on their strong performances.
